info.title: DEXOS Open API v1
info.summary: The standard public interface (REST + WebSocket) for builders, developers and liquidity providers
info.description:
The DEXOS public API for third-party developers, builders and liquidity providers. The specification
lives in `docs/specs/public-api-v1.md`; `docs/research/api-landscape-2026-09.md` compares it with
Hyperliquid, Lighter, Aster and Pacifica. **This document mirrors the gateway's v1 route table**
(`crates/gateway/src/api/v1.rs`, pinned by `scripts/check-openapi.mjs`, INV-API-V1-SPEC-MIRROR).
**Every read endpoint, write endpoint, vault endpoint and WebSocket channel listed here is implemented.**
The only planned items are the timestamp-window nonce (v1.1, an execution-layer change) and the
builder volume projection (§6 of the specification).
The legacy endpoints (`/order`, `/markets`, `/ws`, …, documented at `/docs`) remain available; v1 is a
translation layer on top of them and returns bit-identical data.

## Quick start

1. `GET /v1/exchange` → the EIP-712 domain (`domain` / `chainId`) and the token table (with the numeric
   `token` ids the `Withdrawal` / `Transfer` structs carry); `GET /v1/markets/BTC-USD` → `priceDecimals` /
   `sizeDecimals` and `signingMarketId` (the `market` field of the signed structs).
2. `GET /v1/account/nonce?address=<your address>` → the next `nonce` and `signingAccountId` (the value for the
   `accountId` field of the signed struct; signing is the only thing it is for).
3. Scale `price` and `size` to integers locally (`ticks = price × 10^priceDecimals`,
   `lots = size × 10^sizeDecimals`), sign the `Order(...)` struct (each write endpoint states its
   `x-eip712.typeString`) and `POST /v1/orders`
   `{account, nonce, signature, symbol, side, type: "limit", price, size, clientOrderId?}` →
   `200 {orderId, status: resting|filled|…}` or `422 {error}`.
4. Programmatic trading: approve an API wallet once from the main wallet with
   `POST /v1/account/agents/approve`, then sign with it and pass its address as `signer`
   (the `AgentExec` signature covers the canonical-bytes hash of the inner command). Batch orders,
   cancels, replaces and the dead man's switch all go through the API wallet; **an API wallet cannot
   move funds**.
5. Subscriptions: `GET /v1/ws` → `{"method":"subscribe","params":{"channel":"book","symbol":"BTC-USD"}}`.
   After a disconnect, resume from the last `id` you saw with `/v1/account/fills?after=` or
   `/v1/events?after=`.

## Conventions

- Path prefix `/v1`; JSON; camelCase field names; timestamps in Unix milliseconds; lower-case enums.
- **Prices, sizes and amounts are decimal strings**: `ticks = price × 10^priceDecimals`,
  `lots = size × 10^sizeDecimals` (both must divide exactly); USDC amounts are scaled by `10^6`.
  `priceDecimals` / `sizeDecimals` come from `GET /v1/markets`.
- Markets are addressed by **`symbol`** (`BTC-USD` / `BTC-USDC`), accounts by **`address`**
  (+ `subaccount`, 0 = main account), vaults by **`vault`** (the vault id; v1.1 §4.3). **No v1 response addresses anything by a numeric id.** The numeric ids v1
  does return (`signingAccountId` on `/v1/account/nonce` and `/v1/account/subaccounts`, `signingMarketId` on
  `/v1/markets`, `token` on `/v1/exchange`) exist only because the EIP-712 structs carry them; they are inputs to
  signing, never addresses.
- Every error has the shape `{error:{code, num, message, details?}}`: `code` is a stable string
  (`Gateway*` for the gateway, the `CoreError` variant name for the execution layer), `num` a stable
  number (1xxxx gateway / 2xxxx execution layer). HTTP status: 400 malformed request · 401 bad
  signature · 403 ownership / scope · 404 · 409 · 412 replica behind · 421 wrong node · 422 business
  rejection · 429 rate limited · 5xx.
- Pagination: `?limit=&after=<cursor>` → `{…, next, hasMore}`; execution-history endpoints also
  return a fixed upper bound `upper`, which you pass back unchanged on the following pages.
- Read consistency: write receipts carry `x-dexos-seq`; a **read after a write** sends
  `x-dexos-min-seq` and gets 412 when the replica is behind (same semantics as the legacy API).

## Signing (write endpoints)

All write endpoints share one envelope: `{account, subaccount?, signer?, nonce, expiresAt?, signature,
…business fields}`. The signature is over the existing EIP-712 typed structs (each endpoint states its
`x-eip712.typeString`), with the domain from `GET /v1/exchange`. Prices and sizes inside the struct are
the **scaled integers**: the SDK scales locally and signs, the gateway performs the same scaling for its
pre-check, and the execution layer verifies the signature authoritatively. When `signer` is present the
request is signed by an API wallet (its nonce lives in the agent scope:
`GET /v1/account/nonce?address=&signer=`). API wallets can only trade; every fund-moving endpoint
answers `403 AgentScopeViolation`.

## Write receipts

By default (`ack=result`) the request waits for the fold (at most one epoch) and returns the business
outcome: a single order gets `200` with the order object or `422` with the rejection reason; a batch
always gets `200` with per-item `items[]`. `ack=sequenced` returns only `{seq, sub}` (for
high-frequency clients). If the outcome does not arrive within the budget the response is `202`:
**do not resend**; look it up with `GET /v1/requests/{requestId}`.

## Rate limiting

Two budgets, each a fixed 60-second window counted in request weights:

- **Per IP** — every `/v1/*` request. The IP is the TCP peer of the gateway; behind the deployment's own
  reverse proxy it is the `x-real-ip` that proxy writes. `x-forwarded-for`, and an `x-real-ip` sent by
  anyone other than a trusted proxy, are ignored.
- **Per account** — writes only, charged **after** the signature pre-check passes, keyed by the main wallet
  of the account being acted on (subaccounts share their main wallet's budget). A request that names
  someone else's address cannot pass the pre-check, so it never touches that account's budget.

Weights: reads 1, order book and prices 2, history endpoints 5, writes `1 + floor(n / 40)` where `n` is
the number of orders plus cancels in the request (a replace counts both). Both budgets default to 1200
per minute; the operator can raise either for a given IP or main wallet (market-maker tiers). Every
`/v1/*` response carries `ratelimit: limit=…, remaining=…, reset=…` and `ratelimit-policy: <limit>;w=60`
for the IP budget; a write that reached the account budget also carries
`x-ratelimit-account: limit=…, remaining=…, reset=…`. Exceeding either budget returns
`429 GatewayRateLimited` with `retry-after` and `details.bucket` = `ip` | `account`. API-wallet writes are
pre-checked at the gateway too: a signature that does not recover to `signer` is `401
GatewayBadSignature`; a `signer` with no grant on the account is `403 UnknownAgent`, an expired one
`403 AgentExpired` — none of them is sequenced. Right after approving an API wallet, send
`x-dexos-min-seq` = the approval receipt's `seq` with the first write. The legacy endpoints are not rate
limited (except `POST /subaccount`, which shares the IP budget).

get.description: The single entry point for integrators: the EIP-712 domain, chainId, deposit system address, token table, version fingerprint, `serverTime` and the numeric conventions. **Never hard-code the domain**: after a chain change or a contract redeployment every signature fails with 401 while every read-only call keeps working.
`{serverTime}` in milliseconds. `expiresAt` in signatures is evaluated against it.

Every market **with display metadata** (a market without a symbol does not exist as far as third parties are concerned). Prices and sizes are scaled by `priceDecimals` / `sizeDecimals` into decimal strings and are bit-identical to `/markets` (INV-API-V1-DECIMAL-ROUNDTRIP).

get.description:
last / mark / oracle / best bid and ask / funding rate / open interest, plus rolling 24h statistics (`prevDayPrice`, `change24h`, `high24h`, `low24h`, `volume24h`, `quoteVolume24h`).

The 24h window is anchored at the latest block the analytics projection has seen (`BlockBegun{now_ms}`, the same clock as the candles), not the host wall clock: it is the 1440 one-minute buckets ending with the anchor's bucket, so every 24h field equals a hand calculation over the same window of 1-minute candles. Statistics are cached for at most 5 s. When they are unavailable (analytics store unreachable, or no block projected yet) `window24h` is null and all six 24h fields are null; the live price fields are unaffected.

to.description: Anchor: the latest projected block time, Unix ms

get.description:
Account value, PnL and net inflow over time, plus window statistics, for the performance card of a portfolio page (spec `public-api-v1-1.md` §4.8; compare Hyperliquid `info type=portfolio`, Lighter `/api/v1/pnl`, Aster's portfolio chart). Every point comes from a per-minute account value sample; the curve starts when sampling started for this account (no backfill), buckets without a sample produce no point, and nothing is interpolated.

Two scopes are returned side by side. `perp` = the USDC risk group's net collateral (the same number as `/v1/account` `equity`); USDC moved by spot trades counts as a transfer between perp and spot. `total` = all collateral groups, other token balances valued at the token's latest USDC spot trade price, and vault shares; vault deposits / redemptions are internal moves there. Tokens without a USDC price are excluded and listed in `unvaluedTokens`.

`pnl = accountValue − cumulative net inflow`, so deposits, withdrawals and transfers never show up as PnL. `history[].pnl` and `history[].netInflow` are relative to the first point of the window. When two samples straddle missing execution history, that interval's PnL is not counted (its value change is carried by `netInflow`) and it is listed in `gaps`.

get.description: Look up the outcome of a request by its identity (`0x` + keccak(signer ‖ EIP-712 digest), the `requestId` of every write response). 200: `status` = `executed` / `rejected` (with `seq`, `sub`, `events`, `items`, `nonceConsumed`, `reason` when rejected) or `pending` (sequenced, not yet folded). Otherwise an error whose `details.status` is `not_found` (404: no execution with this id up to `details.asOfSeq`), `conflict` (409: the nonce in `scope`/`nonce` was consumed by a different request, `details.conflictingRequest`) or `history_unavailable` (503: the execution history has gaps, `details.gaps`). Pass `scope` + `nonce` to detect a conflicting nonce; for API-wallet requests add `commandHash` so that, when the history has gaps, the agent nonce can still prove the request did not execute (404 with `details.basis = agent_nonce`). Use it when `ack=result` returned 202.

rules: Snapshot channels (book / bbo / prices / account / positions / orders) send one frame with `isSnapshot:true` on subscribe. book / bbo / prices / account / positions are then coalesced per block: events only mark them, and at each block boundary (`BlockBegun`, about once a second) each is read once and pushed only if its data changed (`isSnapshot:false`). account / positions of an account that holds positions are also re-read when marks or funding move.

orders: the snapshot is all open orders across markets; after it every accept / fill / cancel / expiry is one frame with `clientOrderId` (if any) and `status` (open / filled / canceled / expired). Apply frames idempotently by `orderId`: a snapshot replaces the set, any other frame keeps the order if `status` is `open` and removes it otherwise. Order events already covered by the snapshot's view are not sent.

The candles channel sends one frame per fill with **the latest state of the current bar** (o/h/l/c/v accumulated; clients keep the last frame); a new bar starts automatically when the interval rolls over.

Time-series channels (trades / fills / ledger / events) send one frame per event, carrying `seq` and `data.id`; for fills and ledger `data.id` is the `after` cursor of `/v1/account/fills` and `/v1/account/ledger`.

Resume: the subscribe ack carries the ledger `epoch`; private frames carry `epoch` and `seq`, public book / bbo frames carry `seq`. `lagged{dropped, epoch, upper}` means the server-side broadcast fell behind and frames were dropped; **dropped frames are never resent**. Right after it every snapshot subscription receives one `isSnapshot:true` frame, and fills / ledger frames at or before `upper` are no longer sent: backfill them with `after=<last data.id received>&epoch=<epoch>&upper=<upper>` (retry later on 400 `not yet complete`); the two parts join without gaps or duplicates. If `epoch` changed after a reconnect, rebuild state instead of resuming old cursors.
At most 200 subscriptions per connection; the server closes a connection that has sent no frame (pings count) for 60 s.

Rate limiting: REST uses fixed 60-second windows per IP and, for writes, per main wallet (weights: reads 1, order book / prices 2, history 5, writes 1 + floor(n / 40); default 1200 per minute each); every response carries `ratelimit` / `ratelimit-policy`, writes also `x-ratelimit-account`, and exceeding a budget yields 429 with `retry-after`. The WebSocket connection itself carries no weight.

Private channels are subscribed by `address` (+ optional `subaccount`, default 0) without authentication (the same data is publicly readable over REST; identical to Hyperliquid / Pacifica). Subscribing by `vault` is not supported yet.

Private channels (orders / fills / account / positions / ledger) accept `vault` instead of `address` / `subaccount` (specification v1.1 §4.3; giving both is an error frame); their frames then show `vault` in place of `address` / `subaccount`.

prices.data: `{prices:[Price], ts, window24h}` (same body as `GET /v1/prices`, including the 24h fields)

book.data: Book (`depth` levels per side, 1..=100, default 20; out of range is an error frame)

orders.data: Snapshot: `{address, subaccount, orders:[OpenOrder]}`. Update: `{address, subaccount, orderId, clientOrderId, symbol, event: accepted|fill|canceled|expired, status: open|filled|canceled|expired, side?, price?, size?, filled?, remaining?, lastFilled?, fillId?, ts}`

candles.data: Candle (`{symbol, i, t, T, o, h, l, c, v}`); the current bar is sent on every fill. `interval` takes the same values as REST; an unknown one is an error frame

funding.data: `{symbol, rate, index, ts}`, one frame per funding settlement

ledger.data: LedgerEntry + `address`, `subaccount` (deposits / withdrawals / fees / funding / transfers …); one frame per ledger leg caused by a command

x-error-codes.execution: `20000 + codec error code`; the code table is the CoreError numbering in `crates/core/src/codec.rs` (append-only); the string code is the variant name. Common ones: InsufficientMargin / NonceMismatch / SignatureExpired / AgentScopeViolation / MarketNotTrading / PostOnlyWouldCross / FokInsufficientLiquidity / ReduceOnlyWrongSide / OrderNotAligned / EquityTierLimitExceeded / InvalidLeverage / UnknownOrder / NotOrderOwner.
